A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAP research and contain readable main text, equations, Figures 1–13, and Appendix A.1–A.4. The complete material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, counting, and pose-estimation experiments in Section 4, with additional PPO/HAM comparisons and exploration examples in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including prediction-accuracy and pose-error curves in the main text and additional empirical analyses in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same TAP-SAC and TAP-CrossQ procedures, prediction-loss coupling, reward recomputation, and shared transformer architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Circle-Square, Tactile MNIST, Starstruck, and Toolbox with the same task requirements and simulated environments. Appendix A's coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Figure 4 retains HAM, TAP-RND, and the LSTM variants for Circle-Square; the tactile tasks retain TAP-RND. Appendix Figure 9 retains HAM, PPO/PPO-TAP, PPO-LSTM, and TAP-CrossQ.

E3.justification: The written training budgets, episode lengths, evaluation metrics, and held-out evaluation settings are unchanged. Figure 4's shorter displayed interval does not establish a changed training procedure: Appendix A.1 already states a 250K-step budget in both versions.

E4.justification: The transformer-versus-LSTM ablation, extended PPO/HAM comparison, exploration-efficiency analysis, and qualitative exploration examples are retained. Figure 4's zoom introduces no new analytical question or experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds and retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices, including one-standard-deviation shading in Figure 4. No run counts or statistical procedures change.

E6.justification: Figure 4 truncates the Circle-Square TAP-SAC and TAP-CrossQ trajectories at approximately 250K steps, whereas v1 displays them to nearly 1M. In particular, the later TAP-SAC trajectory is no longer reported. Values over the shared interval, textual numerical findings, and appendix results are unchanged; this is a limited omission of plotted results.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, objective and gradient decomposition in Equations 1–3, critic-loss expression, and appendix classification formulas are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about a task-agnostic active-perception framework, SAC/CrossQ variants, transformer benefits, and empirical effectiveness across four benchmarks.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning off-policy sample reuse, transformer advantages, and CrossQ robustness are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning sample efficiency, absent real-world experiments, and untested scalability.

D1.justification: The acknowledgments newly identify the IAS Compute Cluster as the computation resource. Appendix implementation details and benchmark access information remain unchanged; the new disclosure does not establish a hardware or experimental-setting change.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and all 36 cited works are retained. Bibliography movement reflects page reflow rather than added or removed references.

P1.justification: v2 replaces placeholder acknowledgments with actual funding acknowledgments, supplies the missing corresponding-author email, and makes small Figure 4 wording and panel-title edits. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 enlarges the Circle-Square interval through approximately 250K steps, replacing ticks at 0, 500K, and 1M with 0, 100K, and 200K, and shortens panel titles. Contact and acknowledgment additions produce limited page reflow. Other figures and all appendix pages are visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reporting completeness by replacing template acknowledgments with funding and compute information and supplying author contact details. Figure 4 makes early learning and baseline comparisons easier to inspect, although it omits the later TAP-SAC trajectory. These are limited presentation and documentation gains; the scientific contribution and supporting analyses remain essentially unchanged.
